Which map type is the definitive one (is there one)?

It's impossible to truly represent a 3 dimensional globe on 2d space, but the one most are familiar with is mostly born out of navigation for the latitudes and longitudes. Greenland is enormous in most people's mind. Alsaka is tiny to them. Antarctica is just a blob to them. Texas should overlap most of Europe, yet they dont realize the size differences because of the forced perspective.

The AuthaGraph version was designed for a contest few years back I believe. It's based on an older map that used a much more complex shape to represent true size, but was less elegant. If you look into the math used to pick the 96 points of the Authagraph map, it's quite ingenious in design. There's some small warping of persepctive, but it is very slight relative to any other map while maintaining true sizes to near perfect accuracy. Another function of it is that you can center the map on any section you want instead of the classic euro-centric version most are familiar with. It can be tiled, like the ISS path image, or arranged in a number of different ways while maintaining the lines and sizes. I would call it the best 2d representation possible personally.

Authagraph is based on dymaxion map. These are tissot projections on various world maps. Dymaxion goes for perfect landmass, but is confined to a very specific shape. Authagraph can be infinitely tiled, re-arranged and configured - something no other map can - while also maintaining near perfect sizes.

It limits its distortions to sea areas and is more elegant than dymaxion for me. The ability to maintain a 'normal' map representation (rectangle) without using excess sea/water or voids, like dymaxion, is what really sets it apart for me.
